reading.rationale: The phase I trial reported durable objective radiographic responses (1 complete response and 5 partial responses) in pediatric patients with recurrent BRAF V600E-mutant brain tumors treated with vemurafenib.

Multivariate Cox analysis in esophageal cancer patients demonstrated that the TC/CC genotype of p14ARF (CDKN2A) rs3814960 was significantly associated with decreased overall survival and disease-free survival, directly supporting a poor prognostic outcome.

The quoted passage shows that patients with the MDM2 rs34886328 DEL/A +AA genotype had significantly increased overall survival and disease-free survival (HR < 1), supporting a better prognostic outcome in esophageal cancer.

The quoted passages report a statistically significant association between TrkA expression and shorter survival in colon cancer patient cohorts, with FISH confirming that TrkA expression was partly due to NTRK1 fusions. This observed clinical finding in patient samples supports the claim that NTRK1 fusions are associated with poor prognosis.
The study directly demonstrates that NTRK1 fusion-positive colon cancer cells (KM12) are sensitive to both Lestaurtinib and ARRY-470 in vitro, with CC50 values of 10.7 nM and 3.2 nM, respectively.

The quoted passages document a 21-year-old patient with an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion tumor who achieved a 45% reduction in tumor size and >95% necrosis following entrectinib treatment, directly demonstrating clinical sensitivity.
The detection and confirmation of the LMNA-NTRK1 fusion directly established and reclassified the patient's diagnosis to LPF-NT, supporting its positive diagnostic utility in this soft tissue tumor.

The quoted passages document that among six NSCLC patients with EGFR exon 20 insertions treated with osimertinib, four achieved a partial response and two had stable disease, demonstrating clinical sensitivity.

In in vitro mesothelioma cell lines, BAP1 knockdown was observed to increase sensitivity to both vorinostat and mocetinostat, as evidenced by significantly decreased cell survival and a halved LC50 for vorinostat.

In vitro experiments demonstrated that BAP1-null mesothelioma cell lines (NCI-H28 and NCI-H226) had low HDAC2 expression and exhibited higher LC50 values and increased resistance to mocetinostat compared to wild-type cells. This directly supports the claim of mocetinostat resistance with finding-level certainty in non-human preclinical models.

The quoted passages report that CML patients with cryptic BCR-ABL rearrangements achieved complete cytogenetic response and deep molecular response during imatinib therapy, demonstrating sensitivity to the treatment.

The text documents that a non-responding CML patient developed duplication of the BCR/ABL rearrangement during imatinib therapy without achieving cytogenetic response, supporting BCR/ABL duplication as a mechanism of resistance to imatinib.

The quoted text documents observed objective radiographic responses (1 complete response and 5 partial responses) to vemurafenib among pediatric patients with BRAF V600E-mutant brain tumors, demonstrating treatment efficacy.

In vitro assays demonstrated that Ba/F3 cells expressing HER3-V855A were highly sensitive to growth inhibition by both afatinib and pertuzumab with potent IC50 values. While the mutation was identified in a lung adenocarcinoma patient specimen, testing of therapeutic sensitivity was performed exclusively in cell lines.

The quoted text demonstrates that in 124 patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, the TC/CC genotype of p14ARF (CDKN2A) rs3814960 was significantly associated with decreased overall survival and disease-free survival, confirming a poor prognostic outcome.

The quoted passages demonstrate that esophageal squamous cell carcinoma patients harboring the MDM2 rs34886328 DEL/A + AA genotype showed significantly increased overall survival and disease-free survival. These findings directly support the claim of a better prognostic outcome.

The quoted passages describe a patient with a lipofibromatosis-like neural tumor harboring an NTRK gene rearrangement who experienced a 45% tumor reduction by RECIST criteria and >95% histological necrosis following treatment with entrectinib, supporting sensitivity to the therapy.

The identification of the LMNA-NTRK1 fusion by targeted NGS reclassified the patient's diagnosis to lipofibromatosis-like neural tumor (LPF-NT), demonstrating positive diagnostic evidence for this molecular profile in sarcoma.

The quoted passages establish that the presence of t(5;14)(q31;q32) allows for the diagnosis of B-ALL in patient cases with <20% blast cells according to the WHO classification, confirming its positive diagnostic role in human patients.

The quoted passages document that patients with t(5;14)(q31;q32) B-ALL experienced poor treatment response with high induction failure, elevated minimal residual disease, and high mortality (8 of 14 patients died), directly supporting a poor outcome.
The quoted passages report observed clinical antitumor activity, with four of six EGFR exon 20 insertion-positive NSCLC patients achieving a partial response to osimertinib.

Patient 1 with the EGFR A767_V769dup mutation achieved a partial response (PR) and a progression-free survival of 6.0 months following first-line treatment with osimertinib. This directly demonstrates clinical sensitivity to osimertinib in a patient with lung cancer harboring this mutation.

The quoted passages demonstrate that a patient harboring the EGFR S768_D770dup mutation achieved a partial response (PR) with a progression-free survival of 14.6+ months on osimertinib, and another patient with the same mutation achieved stable disease.

The quoted passages describe a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring both EGFR A763_Y764insFQEA and EGFR T790M who was treated with osimertinib and attained a partial response (PR), demonstrating treatment efficacy.
The quoted passage reports a patient case where EGFR T790M was identified after acquired resistance to gefitinib, demonstrating that T790M mediated resistance to gefitinib.
The text documents that a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR A763_Y764insFQEA achieved a partial response and a PFS of 9.0 months following treatment with gefitinib.
The quoted passages demonstrate that siRNA-mediated knockdown of BAP1 in mesothelioma cells increases sensitivity and decreases cell survival following treatment with vorinostat and mocetinostat.

The quoted passages suggest that mesothelioma cell lines adapted to genetic BAP1 loss exhibit reduced sensitivity and increased resistance to HDAC inhibition. This evidence is derived from in vitro cell line models and framed as a suggestion requiring further confirmation.

The quoted text demonstrates that siRNA-mediated knockdown of HDAC2 sensitizes MSTO-211H mesothelioma cells to both vorinostat and mocetinostat, as evidenced by significantly decreased cell viability and a halved LC50 for vorinostat.

The quoted passages show that constitutively HDAC2-deficient mesothelioma cell lines exhibited higher LC50 values and were more resistant to mocetinostat compared to cells with high HDAC2 expression, providing in vitro cell line evidence supporting resistance.
The quoted text demonstrates that the WWTR1-CAMTA1 fusion was detected in 33 of 35 evaluated patient cases, directly supporting its high diagnostic value in epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.
The study directly identified WWTR1-CAMTA1 fusions in 33 of 35 epithelioid hemangioendothelioma cases, confirming the high diagnostic value of detecting this fusion in patient samples.
The quoted passages confirm the identification of the YAP1-TFE3 fusion by RT-PCR and FISH in patient cases of epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, supporting its diagnostic relevance.

The quoted passages demonstrate the identification of the YAP1-TFE3 fusion by RT-PCR in 2 of 35 human epithelioid hemangioendothelioma cases, supporting its positive diagnostic relevance. These are directly observed findings from patient cases.
The passages report that a CML patient who did not respond to imatinib exhibited BCR/ABL duplication, confirming this alteration as a mechanism of resistance to TKI therapy.

The quoted passages report that 5 out of 6 Ph-negative CML patients achieved CCgR and/or MMR during TKI therapy with outcomes similar to Ph-positive patients. This observed clinical response directly supports the claim of sensitivity to TKIs in patients with cryptic BCR-ABL fusions.

The passages report promising anti-tumor activity and efficacy of vemurafenib in children with recurrent BRAF V600E-positive brain tumors/gliomas. This directly supports sensitivity/response, although the wording is somewhat qualified by terms such as “promising” and “efficacious.”

In 124 ESCC patients who underwent radical resection, the p14ARF/CDKN2A rs3814960 TC/CC genotype was significantly associated with decreased overall and disease-free survival after multivariable adjustment. This supports a prognostic poor-outcome association for the variant genotype, although the evidence is for the TC/CC genotype rather than rs3814960 without genotype specification.

In 124 ESCC patients who underwent radical resection, the MDM2 rs34886328 DEL/A + AA genotype was associated with significantly increased overall and disease-free survival (HR 0.27 and 0.22, respectively, with multiple-testing-adjusted P values significant). This directly supports a better prognostic outcome, although the paper notes that larger-population validation is needed.

Human colon cancer patient cohorts showed that TrkA/NTRK1 overexpression was significantly associated with shorter or poorer overall survival. Although described as marginal, the observed association supports prognostic poor outcome.

In a human patient with an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion and lipofibromatosis-like neural tumor, entrectinib produced a 45% tumor reduction and >95% necrosis, with sufficient response to enable surgery. These are observed clinical and pathological responses supporting sensitivity to entrectinib.

The passages report that NSCLC patients with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations treated with osimertinib experienced partial responses or stable disease, with four patients attaining partial response. Although the authors qualify activity as occurring in certain mutation subtypes and call for further study, the observed patient results support sensitivity/response.

The quoted experiments show that BAP1 depletion increases mesothelioma cell sensitivity to vorinostat and mocetinostat, including a lower vorinostat LC50. This is an observed in-vitro cell-line result, not evidence from patients.

The study reports WWTR1-CAMTA1 fusion genes in 33 of 35 EHE cases and explicitly states that detecting EHE fusion genes has high diagnostic value. This supports a positive diagnostic association for the molecular profile in malignant epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

The study reports YAP1-TFE3 fusion in 2 of 35 human EHE cases and states that fusion-gene detection has high diagnostic value. This supports the diagnostic association, although it does not establish that the fusion is present in all cases.

The passages report that patients with cryptic BCR-ABL rearrangements in Ph-negative CML achieved complete cytogenetic and/or major molecular responses after TKI therapy, with outcomes similar to Ph-positive CML. This is an observed patient response supporting sensitivity to TKIs.

The passages report therapy resistance in a human CML patient with duplication of the BCR/ABL rearrangement and explicitly identify BCR/ABL duplication as a mechanism of TKI resistance. The study is small, but the reported association is an observed patient finding.

The conclusion reports promising anti-tumor activity of vemurafenib in children with recurrent BRAF V600E-positive brain tumors, supporting sensitivity/response in the claimed disease and molecular profile. However, “promising” is hedged rather than a definitive observed response statement.

The passages report that vemurafenib was tolerable and efficacious, with promising anti-tumor efficacy, in children with recurrent or progressive BRAF V600E-mutant gliomas. This directly supports sensitivity/response, although the wording “promising” is somewhat qualified.

The passages report that ERBB3/HER3 V855A is highly sensitive to afatinib and pertuzumab and describe the mutation as a predictive marker for response to HER-targeted therapy in NSCLC. However, the supporting response data are primarily from transformed cell lines and biological assays, with a patient tumor sample establishing the mutation but no documented patient treatment response.

In 124 ESCC patients treated with radical resection, CDKN2A/p14ARF rs3814960 TC/CC was significantly associated with decreased overall and disease-free survival, with adjusted hazard ratios above 2. This directly supports a prognostic poor-outcome association, although the authors note the findings require validation.

In 124 ESCC patients undergoing radical resection, the MDM2 rs34886328 DEL/A +AA genotype was associated with significantly increased overall and disease-free survival (HR 0.27 and 0.22; P<0.001). This directly supports a better prognostic outcome in esophageal cancer.

The passage identifies the MDM2 rs34886328 DEL/DEL genotype as an “unfavorable” genotype associated with worse prognosis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma patients. Multivariate analyses report substantially higher hazards for overall and disease-free survival among patients carrying unfavorable genotypes, supporting poor outcome as prognostic significance.

The passage reports that Korean patients with TrkA-positive colon cancer had significantly shorter overall survival than TrkA-negative patients, supporting a poor-outcome prognostic association. The result is explicitly described as marginal but statistically significant and comes from human patient cohorts.

The passage reports that Korean and Chinese colon cancer patients with NTRK1 fusion-driven TrkA expression had poor overall survival. This directly supports a prognostic association between NTRK1 fusion and poor outcome in colon cancer.

In vitro experiments in the NTRK1-fusion-positive colon cancer cell line KM12 showed sensitivity to ARRY-470 and Lestaurtinib, and the authors reported that TrkA-specific inhibitors could provide a treatment strategy for NTRK1 fusion-positive colon cancer. This is cell-line evidence rather than evidence from patients.

The passage describes a human patient with an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion and LP-NFT who received entrectinib, had a robust clinical response, and showed >95% tumor necrosis, directly supporting sensitivity/response.

The quoted human tumor sample showed an LMNA exon 2–NTRK1 exon 11 fusion, confirmed by orthogonal RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing, and the authors state that identifying it reclassified the lesion as an S-100-positive lipofibromatosis-like neural tumor. This directly supports the diagnostic association of an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion with the stated disease.

The passage describes a human patient with an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion and LP-NFT who received entrectinib, had a robust clinical response, and showed >95% tumor necrosis, demonstrating sensitivity to therapy.

In a human spinal tumor sample, sequencing identified an LMNA exon 2–NTRK1 exon 11 in-frame fusion, confirmed by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing. The authors state that this fusion reclassified the diagnosis as S-100-positive lipofibromatosis-like neural tumor.

Human patient data show frequent induction failure, high MRD, and substantial mortality, and the authors explicitly characterize treatment response as poor. However, the paper describes the overall prognosis as intermediate rather than definitively poor.

The passage reports observed partial responses and stable disease in NSCLC patients with certain EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations treated with osimertinib, indicating antitumor activity. The conclusion is limited to certain EGFRex20ins subtypes rather than all such mutations.

The passage reports that a patient with EGFR A767_V769dup treated with first-line osimertinib achieved a partial response (PR) with 6.0 months of progression-free survival. This is a direct observed clinical response in a human patient.

The passages report human patients with EGFR S768_D770dup receiving osimertinib and achieving partial response (patient 2) or stable disease (patient 4), with prolonged progression-free survival. This directly supports clinical sensitivity/response in non-small-cell lung cancer.

The quoted passage reports that a human patient with EGFR N771_P772insL non-small-cell lung cancer received first-line osimertinib and achieved stable disease for 4.9 months, an observed clinical response consistent with sensitivity/response, though not tumor shrinkage.

The passage explicitly reports that osimertinib treatment was effective in a patient with EGFR A763_Y764insFQEA and EGFR T790M, supporting sensitivity/response in NSCLC. Although it also describes T790M as a potential resistance mechanism to gefitinib, the osimertinib response is stated as an observed clinical result.

The passage describes a human NSCLC patient in whom EGFR T790M was identified after acquired resistance to gefitinib and states that T790M mediated that resistance. Although it calls T790M a potential mechanism, the quoted case reports an observed resistance association.
The passage describes a human lung adenocarcinoma patient with EGFR A763_Y764insFQEA who received gefitinib and achieved a partial response with a PFS of 9.0 months.

The passage reports that BAP1 knockdown in mesothelioma cells increased sensitivity to HDAC inhibition, with decreased survival after vorinostat or mocetinostat. This is an observed in-vitro cell-line result, not evidence from patients.

The passage suggests that mesothelioma cells with genetic BAP1 loss adapt and show reduced sensitivity to HDAC inhibitors, supporting resistance. However, it explicitly presents this as a suggested finding requiring confirmation, based on cell-line data rather than patients.

The passage reports that HDAC2-depleted mesothelioma cells showed significantly decreased viability after treatment with vorinostat and mocetinostat, indicating sensitivity to HDAC inhibitors. This is an in-vitro cell-line finding, not evidence from patients.

The passage reports that constitutively HDAC2-deficient mesothelioma cell lines had higher mocetinostat LC50 values and greater residual viability than HDAC2-high cells, indicating resistance. This is an observed in-vitro cell-line finding, not patient evidence.

In human EHE cases, WWTR1-CAMTA1 fusions were detected in 33 of 35 tested cases, and the paper explicitly describes fusion testing as having high diagnostic value. This supports a positive diagnostic association for WWTR1-CAMTA1 in malignant epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

In human EHE cases, WWTR1-CAMTA1 fusion was detected in 33 of 35 fusion-positive cases, and the authors state that identifying these fusions has high diagnostic value. The passages directly support the fusion as a diagnostic molecular profile for malignant epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

The study reports YAP1-TFE3 fusion in 2 of 35 human EHE cases and states that detecting EHE fusion genes has high diagnostic value. This directly supports the diagnostic association, although it does not address therapy.

The study reports YAP1-TFE3 fusions in 2 of 35 human EHE cases and states that fusion-gene detection has high diagnostic value and provides important diagnostic information. This supports a positive diagnostic association for YAP1-TFE3 with epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

The passages report that a patient with duplicated BCR/ABL rearrangement was a nonresponder or developed therapy resistance during imatinib/TKI treatment, and explicitly identify duplication as a resistance mechanism. The evidence is from human CML patients and describes observed clinical outcomes.

The quoted evidence directly demonstrates that vemurafenib is efficacious in children with BRAF V600E mutant brain gliomas, with documented clinical responses (1 CR, 5 PR) and stable disease, with responses remaining durable for over 40 months, confirming sensitivity and response to the therapy.

In vitro experiments demonstrate that Ba/F3 cells expressing HER3-V855A show sensitivity to afatinib and pertuzumab (IC50 values <1 nmol/L and <1 μg/mL) and weaker sensitivity to erlotinib (IC50 344±4 nmol/L). The authors explicitly state the mutation 'may predict response to targeted therapy,' supporting the predictive sensitivity claim, though the clinical applicability is characterized as a possibility rather than proven in patients.

A patient with V855A demonstrated disease progression on VIDE treatment (clinical evidence), and the paper states trastuzumab is ineffective against V855A based on unpublished experimental data. The evidence is mixed in source—clinical for VIDE, experimental for trastuzumab—and the trastuzumab finding cannot be verified from the published report.

The evidence demonstrates that the TC/CC genotype of p14ARF rs3814960 is significantly associated with decreased overall survival (HR=2.77, p=0.006) and disease-free survival in esophageal cancer patients, directly supporting the claim of poor prognostic outcome.

The quoted passage directly reports that patients with the DEL/A +AA genotype of MDM2 rs34886328 had notably increased overall survival and disease-free survival, with hazard ratios less than 1 indicating reduced mortality risk. This directly supports the claim of a better prognostic outcome for this variant in esophageal cancer patients.

The passage explicitly defines MDM2 rs34886328 DEL/DEL as an 'unfavorable' genotype associated with worse prognosis in esophageal cancer patients. Multivariate Cox proportional hazard analyses demonstrate significantly elevated hazard ratios (12.62 for OS and 13.09 for DFS when combined with another unfavorable genotype) with p-values <0.001, directly supporting poor outcome association.

Both quoted passages directly report observed findings from colon cancer patient cohorts demonstrating that high TrkA expression/overexpression is significantly associated with poorer overall survival, which supports the claim that NTRK1 TrkA overexpression has poor prognostic significance. The evidence includes survival analysis with quantified hazard ratios from 216 Korean colon cancer patients.

The quoted evidence demonstrates that KM12, a colon cancer cell line harboring TPM3-NTRK1 fusion, shows sensitivity to Lestaurtinib (CC50 10.7 nM), ARRY-470 (CC50 3.2 nM), and Crizotinib (CC50 184.8 nM), supporting the predictive value of this molecular profile for therapeutic response. Although the fusion was identified in Korean patient samples, the therapeutic sensitivity data cited comes from cell line experiments.

The quoted passages document a patient with LMNA-NTRK1 fusion in a mesenchymal cell neoplasm (LP-NFT) who achieved a robust clinical response to entrectinib, with post-operative pathology revealing >95% necrosis demonstrating exceptional inhibitor sensitivity. This directly confirms the predictive sensitivity/response relationship claimed between the molecular profile and therapy.

The quoted passages document a patient with LMNA-NTRK1 fusion in a mesenchymal spindle cell neoplasm who demonstrated robust clinical response to entrectinib, with post-operative pathology revealing >95% necrosis, directly supporting the predictive claim of sensitivity/response to this therapy.

The quoted evidence strongly supports the molecular profile (LMNA-NTRK1 fusion), disease (mesenchymal cell neoplasm), evidence type (diagnostic), and positive clinical significance. However, it directly contradicts the claim that therapies are 'none'—the first quote explicitly states the patient was treated with the NTRK inhibitor entrectinib in a clinical trial with exceptional clinical response and sustained remission.

The quoted passages confirm the LMNA-NTRK1 fusion, mesenchymal spindle cell neoplasm, and positive diagnostic/clinical significance. However, they directly contradict the claim's statement of "Therapies: none" by explicitly describing successful treatment with the NTRK inhibitor entrectinib, including >95% necrosis and sustained remission at 12 months post-operatively.

The quoted evidence explicitly states that the t(5;14)(q31;q32) translocation "permitted a diagnosis" of B-ALL in cases with low blast infiltration, and identifies t(5;14)(q31;q32); IGH-IL3 as a distinct diagnostic entity. The evidence describes established clinical observations from patient cases, confirming the diagnostic significance of this molecular profile.

The quoted passages explicitly establish that t(5;14)(q31;q32); IGH-IL3 rearrangement is diagnostic for B-ALL, with the first quote directly stating the translocation 'permitted a diagnosis' of this disease. The evidence confirms the molecular profile, disease entity, and diagnostic significance, derived from clinical observations of patient cases and their characteristics.

The quoted evidence directly reports clinical outcomes from NSCLC patients with EGFRex20ins mutations treated with osimertinib, documenting four patients achieving partial response and two achieving stable disease, which demonstrates sensitivity and clinical response supporting the claim.
Patient 1 with the EGFR A767_V769dup mutation received osimertinib and achieved partial response with a PFS of 6.0 months, demonstrating clinical sensitivity to the drug.

Patient 2 with EGFR S768_D770dup achieved partial response to osimertinib with 14.6+ months PFS, and patient 4 harboring the same mutation achieved stable disease with 11.2+ months PFS. Both patients remained on osimertinib treatment, directly demonstrating clinical sensitivity to osimertinib in patients with this EGFR mutation.

Patient 3 with EGFR N771_P772insL achieved only stable disease on osimertinib and required treatment change after 4.9 months due to progressive disease (enlarged pleural nodules), which does not demonstrate sensitivity or durable response to the therapy.

The quoted passages describe Patient 5's clinical response to osimertinib (initial improvement and tumor shrinkage) in lung adenocarcinoma, but do not specify Patient 5's EGFR mutation type, so the connection to the claimed D770_N771insG mutation is not established in these excerpts.

Patient 6 harboring EGFR A763_Y764insFQEA received gefitinib as first-line treatment and achieved partial response with 9.0 months progression-free survival, directly demonstrating clinical sensitivity and response to gefitinib for this specific mutation in lung adenocarcinoma.

The passage identifies EGFR T790M in a patient who developed acquired resistance to gefitinib and describes it as a "potential resistant mechanism" in NSCLC patients, supporting the claim of T790M-associated gefitinib resistance. The use of "potential" moderates the certainty of the mechanism.

The quoted evidence describes Patient 6, a lung adenocarcinoma case with both EGFR A763_Y764insFQEA and EGFR T790M mutations, who achieved partial response (PR) to osimertinib treatment, directly demonstrating clinical sensitivity to this therapy for this molecular profile in non-small cell lung cancer.

The quoted evidence directly demonstrates that BAP1 depletion increases sensitivity of mesothelioma cells to both vorinostat and mocetinostat, with BAP1 knockdown reducing vorinostat LC50 from 2.6 μM to 1.2 μM and decreasing cell survival. However, these findings are limited to in vitro cell line studies rather than clinical patient data.

The quoted passages demonstrate that HDAC2 depletion (via siRNA) increases sensitivity to both vorinostat and mocetinostat in mesothelioma cell lines, with reduced LC50 values shown for vorinostat. However, the evidence is complicated by the observation that constitutively HDAC2-deficient cell lines exhibit resistance to mocetinostat, suggesting the predictive relationship may be context-dependent or subject to adaptive mechanisms.

The quoted passages directly report that constitutively HDAC2-deficient mesothelioma cell lines were more resistant to mocetinostat than HDAC2-high cells, with measured LC50 values 1.7–2.0-fold higher. This observed experimental result directly supports the claim that low HDAC2 expression predicts mocetinostat resistance.

Both quoted passages demonstrate that mesothelioma cells with genetic BAP1 loss exhibit reduced sensitivity to HDAC inhibitors including mocetinostat. Quote 1 directly states that cells with genetic BAP1 loss show reduced HDAC inhibitor sensitivity, and Quote 2 shows mesothelioma cell lines with constitutively low HDAC2 (a consequence of BAP1 loss) are significantly more resistant to mocetinostat with higher LC50 values (4.0-4.9 μM vs. 2.4 μM).

Quote 1 directly establishes that WWTR1-CAMTA1 fusion is present in 33 of 35 evaluable EHE cases (94%), confirming the molecular-disease association. Quote 2 explicitly states that identifying fusion genes in EHE provides "important diagnostic information," supporting the diagnostic significance claim.

The first quote directly demonstrates that WWTR1-CAMTA1 fusion was identified in 33 of 35 evaluable EHE cases (94%), establishing its presence in the disease. The second quote explicitly states that fusion gene identification provides important diagnostic information in EHE, supporting both the molecular-diagnostic association and its positive clinical significance.

The first quote directly identifies YAP1-TFE3 fusion in 2 of 35 epithelioid hemangioendothelioma cases, confirming the molecular profile and disease association. The second quote explicitly states that fusion gene identification "provides important diagnostic information," supporting the diagnostic evidence type and positive clinical significance. The therapies aspect is not addressed in the quoted passages.

The first quote directly confirms YAP1-TFE3 fusion was identified in 2 of 35 EHE cases (6%), establishing the molecular profile in this disease. The second quote confirms fusion genes provide important diagnostic information in EHE, supporting the diagnostic clinical significance claimed.

The quoted evidence reports that 21/21 cases were positive for ERG and that ERG and FLI1 showed expression in all cases examined and are helpful in highlighting the vascular nature of EHE, directly supporting ERG expression as a diagnostic marker for epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

The quoted evidence directly demonstrates FLI1 positivity in epithelioid hemangioendothelioma cases (5/5 cases tested showed positive results) and confirms FLI1's diagnostic utility in highlighting the vascular nature of the disease. This finding supports the claim of FLI1 expression as a diagnostic marker with positive clinical significance in EHE.

PECAM1 is synonymous with CD31. The quoted evidence demonstrates membranous CD31 expression in all 39 cases of epithelioid hemangioendothelioma and identifies CD31 as a diagnostic marker for highlighting the vascular nature of the disease.

The quoted passages directly document that INI1 protein was retained in epithelioid hemangioendothelioma patient samples, with one statement reporting retention in all 3 samples tested and another confirming retention "as shown in some of our cases." This directly supports the claimed molecular profile of retained INI1 expression in this disease.

The quoted passages report that Ph-neg CML patients with cryptic BCR/ABL fusion achieved molecular and cytogenetic responses to imatinib and nilotinib, with 5 out of 6 patients achieving CCgR and/or MMR during TKI treatment. These observed clinical outcomes directly support the claim that this molecular profile predicts sensitivity and response to these therapies.

The quoted passages document Ph-negative CML patients with BCR/ABL rearrangement achieving complete cytogenetic response and major molecular response with imatinib and nilotinib, with 5 out of 6 patients achieving CCgR and/or MMR during TKI treatment, directly demonstrating sensitivity and response to these therapies.

The quoted passages directly describe CML patients with BCR/ABL duplication who failed imatinib and TKI therapy, explicitly stating that duplication is "a mechanism of resistance to the therapy" in both treatment eras. Multiple patients with this duplication did not achieve clinical response.

The quoted passages directly demonstrate that BCR/ABL duplication is associated with resistance to imatinib and TKIs, describing it as an established 'mechanism of resistance to the therapy' in clinical cases where patients failed to achieve cytogenetic response.

The evidence documents BCR/ABL duplication in a CML patient (patient n.2) during disease progression and associates it with adverse clinical outcome through patient case data. However, the paper attributes the poor outcome primarily to Sokal risk stratification rather than independently establishing duplication as the prognostic determinant.

The evidence documents BCR/ABL duplication in CML patients during disease progression with clonal evolution and increased transcript (quote 1), and shows association with adverse clinical outcome in a patient with intermediate Sokal risk who exhibited the duplication (quotes 2-3), supporting the prognostic significance for poor outcome.

The quoted passage reports that BCR/ABL rearrangement was detected by RT-PCR analysis at diagnosis in CML patients, directly confirming the diagnostic role of BCR/ABL rearrangement in chronic myeloid leukemia stated in the claim.

The quoted evidence directly documents BCR/ABL rearrangement detected by RT-PCR in 398 CML cases at diagnosis, supporting the molecular profile, disease identification, and diagnostic evidence type. The context mentions TKIs therapy, indicating treatments are addressed in the paper.

The quoted passages identify 2 CML patients (n.1 and n.3) with ABL1 deletions adjacent to BCR/ABL breakpoints and document that both achieved molecular responses to imatinib therapy (Complete CgR and Major Molecular Response). This demonstrates an observed association between the specified molecular profile and imatinib sensitivity in these patient cases.

The quoted evidence identifies patients with BCR deletions adjacent to BCR/ABL breakpoints (quote 1) and directly demonstrates that these same patients (n.1 and n.3) responded well to imatinib therapy, achieving Complete Cytogenetic Response within 24 months (quote 2) and Major Molecular Response (quote 3). This observed clinical response associates the molecular profile with sensitivity to imatinib therapy.

The quoted evidence describes a Phase I clinical trial showing vemurafenib produced objective responses (1 complete response, 5 partial responses, 13 stable disease) in 19 children with BRAF V600E mutant brain gliomas, with the authors explicitly concluding that vemurafenib is efficacious in this population.

The quoted evidence demonstrates in-vitro sensitivity of HER3-V855A-expressing cells to both afatinib and pertuzumab, with superior growth inhibition compared to wild-type cells. However, the clinical predictive significance is expressed with cautious language: the mutation "may predict response" and provides "biological rationale" for establishing it as a predictive marker, rather than directly confirming predictive utility in patients.

The quoted evidence demonstrates that KM12, a colon cancer cell line harboring NTRK1 fusion, was sensitive to both Lestaurtinib and ARRY-470 with low CC50 values (10.7 nM and 3.2 nM respectively), directly supporting the claim of sensitivity/response to these therapies in NTRK1 fusion-positive colon cancer. The findings are based on cell line studies rather than clinical patient data.

Both quoted passages report observed results from human patients demonstrating that high TrkA expression or TrkA-positive status is significantly associated with shorter survival time and poorer overall survival in colon cancer patients, directly supporting the claim of poor prognostic outcome.

The quoted passages describe an actual patient with NTRK-rearranged lipofibromatosis-like neural tumor who demonstrated excellent clinical response to entrectinib (45% tumor size reduction and >95% post-operative necrosis), directly demonstrating that NTRK fusion status predicts sensitivity to entrectinib therapy.

The quoted evidence reports detection and confirmation of a LMNA-NTRK1 fusion via NGS and orthogonal RT-PCR/Sanger sequencing in patient tumor tissue, with this fusion directly enabling diagnosis of lipofibromatosis-like neural tumor. This establishes both the molecular profile and disease association claimed.

The quoted passage directly affirms that the t(5;14)(q31;q32) translocation has diagnostic significance for B-ALL, stating it "allows diagnosis" according to WHO classification, which supports the claim's diagnostic evidence type and positive clinical significance.
The quoted evidence directly states that t(5;14)(q31;q32) allows diagnosis of B-ALL cases according to WHO classification, which supports the diagnostic significance of this molecular profile.

The quoted passages document poor treatment response with frequent induction failure and high MRD levels, and report 8/14 patients (57%) deceased in the outcome cohort, directly demonstrating the poor prognosis associated with this IGH-IL3 rearrangement.

The quoted passages explicitly state that "Response to treatment is poor" with frequent induction failures and high MRD levels, and report that 8 out of 14 patients with available outcome data died, demonstrating poor clinical outcomes. This directly supports the claim of poor prognosis for this B-ALL subtype.

All three quotes report clinical results from NSCLC patients with EGFR exon 20 insertions treated with osimertinib, demonstrating objective responses (67.7% partial response rate with 100% disease control) and antitumor activity. The evidence directly supports that osimertinib produces sensitivity/response in this patient population.

The quoted evidence reports that Patient 1 with EGFR A767_V769dup achieved partial response to osimertinib with a PFS of 6.0 months, directly demonstrating clinical sensitivity to this therapy for this specific mutation in a non-small cell lung cancer patient.
